description: Fix all five user-reported issues on the fix/scene-and-voice-polish branch, each grounded in the measured diagnosis in context.json. (1) Reframe the pet so its head faces the camera. (2) Make the chef gesture visibly with its arms while speaking (diagnose runtime, root-cause, fix) and improve the coach's whole-group talking motion (coach is an unrigged OBJ with NO arm bones — surface this honestly). (3) De-robotize chef+coach Web Speech voices within Web Speech limits (flag that true neural TTS needs a new dependency). (4) Give the wardrobe avatar more stage space. (5) Remove the Migration Control Plane card. Then capture AFTER evidence and preserve all WS1-WS4 wins.
steps: ISSUE 5 (trivial, do first): In lib/data.ts delete the FIRST entry of the projects: Project[] array (tag 'AWS', title 'Migration Control Plane', meta 'Landing-zone & cost telemetry', label 'PROJECT SHOT · Cloud Migration dashboard', no href). Leave the 'On-Prem to AWS Cloud Migration' entry in the cases array untouched. app/page.tsx needs NO change (it maps over projects; this card uses the generic no-href branch). Confirm the gallery still renders the remaining four cards after build.

ISSUE 1 (pet framing) in components/pet/PetScene.tsx: The schnauzer's long axis (nose-to-tail) runs along X and its narrow width along Z, but the camera looks down -Z, so today it faces the dog's flank. In the model useMemo, apply a Y rotation of ~+/-Math.PI/2 to the recenter root (the inner <primitive>/model group that carries the recenter offset, NOT the animated groupRef whose identity rest the useFrame absolute-offset math relies on) so the nose faces +Z toward the camera; optionally add a small yaw (~15-25deg) for a three-quarter view. CRITICAL: recompute the Box3 recenter AFTER applying the rotation so the rotated model stays centered on the aim point. Determine the correct sign (+ or - PI/2) empirically via a screenshot — do NOT eyeball-guess; the head must be visible and the dog must read front/three-quarter, not side-on. Keep the CameraRig PINNED_CAM/PINNED_LOOK additive-offset math valid and the reducedMotion gate intact. If AIM_HEIGHT/CAMERA_DISTANCE need adjusting to frame the head, that is allowed but must be justified by a before/after screenshot.

ISSUE 2a (chef arms) in components/chef/ChefScene.tsx + verify propagation via components/chef/ChefChatbot.tsx: The measured facts (in context.json) are that all arm bones resolve on the cloned FBX and writing bone.rotation updates the skeleton, so the names/rig are NOT the bug. Re-confirm at runtime that the gesture offsets are actually applied while speaking (e.g. a temporary headless harness that mounts the Avatar, forces speaking=true, and logs an arm bone's rotation across several frames to prove gestureRef eases toward 1 and offsets are non-zero — remove any temp harness before committing). Root-cause WHY the user perceives no motion and FIX it so the chef VISIBLY gesticulates while replying: increase the arm oscillation amplitudes to a clearly visible range that still reads within the fixed head-and-torso framing and never flails/clips, and ensure the speaking window reliably drives gestureRef. Keep the reduced-motion gate working (gTarget = reducedMotion ? 0 : speaking ? 1 : 0 — arms damp to captured rest under reduced motion). Report exactly what you measured (bone names present, whether speaking flips true, whether offsets are applied) and the true root cause.

ISSUE 2b (coach) in components/coach/CoachScene.tsx: The coach OBJ is UNRIGGED (zero bones) — arms cannot move. Do NOT invent a rig. Make the existing whole-group talking motion more believable and clearly visible while speaking (e.g. a bit more pronounced bob + sway + lean, and/or an added gesture-like tilt), consistent with how the scene already animates the group, keeping the reduced-motion freeze and the CameraRig math intact. Clearly state in findings that the coach has no arm rig so real arm motion is not possible and describe what you did instead.

ISSUE 3 (voices): In lib/chef/chefVoice.ts move the utterance params away from the robotic extreme: raise pitch from 0.7 toward natural (~0.95-1.0) and keep rate natural (~0.95-1.0) so the chef no longer sounds like a robot (keep any desired accent preference but stop the extreme low pitch). In BOTH lib/chef/chefVoice.ts and lib/coach/coachVoice.ts, improve pickVoice() to PREFER higher-quality/natural voices and AVOID the lowest-quality fallback: prefer named enhanced/cloud voices (e.g. names containing 'google','natural','enhanced','premium','neural', or well-known high-quality OS voices) and/or prefer voices where localService === false when available, falling back gracefully to any en-* voice then the platform default; keep selection robust across browsers and never gate speaking on availability. MUST keep the onStart/onEnd speaking-window callbacks AND every anti-stuck-engine mitigation (deferred speak, resume(), watchdog, retained this.current, conditional cancel) intact. Keep it fully client-side and static-export safe. Do NOT add any TTS dependency or audio asset. In findings, honestly state what is achievable within Web Speech vs what would require a new dependency (a genuine neural voice), and note that you deliberately did NOT add one.

ISSUE 4 (wardrobe) in components/WardrobeBuilder.tsx and/or components/wardrobe/WardrobeScene.tsx: Give the 3D stage more room and/or frame the avatar larger. Options: widen the center grid column and/or narrow the side menu columns in the lg:grid-cols template, and/or raise the stage min-height (currently min-h-[420px] and container minHeight:760), and/or adjust the WardrobeScene camera framing (fov/distance/target) so the avatar fills the stage better. Constraints: NO horizontal scroll and no covered controls at 390x844 (WS4), OrbitControls turntable/zoom must still work, the reduced-motion autoRotate gate must stay. Verify at BOTH 390x844 and 1280x900.
Rebuild: npm run build (static export must still succeed, all five routes prerender).

Capture AFTER evidence under docs/fixes/ mirroring the BEFORE labels: after-pet (1280), after-chef (1280), after-coach (1280), after-wardrobe (390 and 1280). For the chef arm-motion proof, capture a still with the chef mid-gesture (drive speaking true via a scripted interaction/query if the harness allows, otherwise document the runtime measurement of applied arm offsets alongside the still). Also capture a reduced-motion proof shot for pet or chef to show gestures/motion damp (optional but preferred).

Preserve WS1-WS4: confirm asset() still wraps every public URL touched, quality.ts High/Fast + single QualityToggle untouched, ACESFilmic tone mapping unchanged on all four scenes, engine/state/wardrobeOptions click routing unchanged, reduced-motion gating via useReducedMotion.ts intact, canvas role='img' aria-labels intact, scenes still behind next/dynamic { ssr:false }.
Run npm run lint (only the known font warning allowed).

Commit source + AFTER evidence: git add the changed source files and docs/fixes, then git commit -m 'fix: pet framing, chef gestures, coach motion, voice tuning, wardrobe stage, remove Migration card'. Never stage node_modules/.next/out/assets-src.
acceptance_criteria: lib/data.ts no longer contains the Migration Control Plane project entry; the landing gallery renders the remaining four project cards; the cases 'On-Prem to AWS Cloud Migration' entry is untouched.
In a built/rendered pet scene the schnauzer faces the camera front/three-quarter with its HEAD visible (proven by after-pet screenshot vs before-pet).

The chef visibly gesticulates with its arms while speaking (proven by a mid-gesture still and/or a runtime measurement showing non-zero arm offsets while speaking), and arms damp to rest under reduced motion; findings state the measured root cause.
The coach's whole-group talking motion is clearly visible while speaking; findings honestly state the coach OBJ is unrigged so arm motion is not possible.

chefVoice.ts no longer uses pitch 0.7 (uses a natural pitch ~0.95-1.0); both voices prefer higher-quality voices and avoid the lowest-quality fallback; onStart/onEnd and anti-stuck-engine mitigations are intact; no TTS dependency/asset added; findings state the Web-Speech limitation.

The wardrobe avatar stage is larger; no horizontal scroll and no covered controls at 390x844; OrbitControls and reduced-motion autoRotate gate still work (proven by after-wardrobe screenshots at 390 and 1280).
npm run lint shows only the known font warning; npm run build succeeds and prerenders all five routes.
WS1-WS4 wins preserved (asset() on public URLs, quality/QualityToggle, ACESFilmic, engine click routing, reduced-motion gating, canvas aria-labels, ssr:false).
verification: npm run build (static export succeeds, 5 routes prerender)

node scripts/measure-viewports.mjs for after-pet/after-chef/after-coach/after-wardrobe under docs/fixes and visually confirm pet head faces camera and wardrobe avatar is larger with no horizontal scroll (JSON noHorizontalScroll true at 390 and 1280)
grep confirms 'Migration Control Plane' no longer present in the repo source
Read chefVoice.ts to confirm pitch is no longer 0.7 and both voice pickers prefer quality voices while keeping callbacks + mitigations

findings.issue5_card: Deleted the FIRST entry of projects[] in lib/data.ts (tag 'AWS', title 'Migration Control Plane', meta 'Landing-zone & cost telemetry', label 'PROJECT SHOT · Cloud Migration dashboard', no href). No app/page.tsx change needed — it maps over projects and this card used the generic no-href branch. grep confirms 'Migration Control Plane' no longer appears anywhere in source. The cases[] 'On-Prem to AWS Cloud Migration' entry is untouched. projects[] now has 4 entries (Coach, Chef, Wardrobe, Pet) and the landing gallery renders the remaining four cards.
findings.issue1_pet: components/pet/PetScene.tsx. Root cause matched the diagnosis: the schnauzer's nose-to-tail axis runs along X (narrow width along Z) but the fixed camera looks down -Z, so it faced the flank (tail toward camera, head turned away). FIX: added `const BODY_YAW = Math.PI / 2 + degToRad(8)` and set `root.rotation.y = BODY_YAW` on the INNER recenter root inside the model useMemo, AFTER scaling and BEFORE the recenter Box3 (so the Box3 recenter is recomputed on the rotated model and it stays centered on the aim point). The animated groupRef is left at identity rest, so the useFrame ABSOLUTE-offset math and the CameraRig PINNED_CAM/PINNED_LOOK additive math remain valid; reducedMotion gate untouched. ROTATION SIGN CHOSEN: +PI/2 (positive), determined EMPIRICALLY via after-pet screenshots — +PI/2 swings the denser head end (-X) toward +Z/the camera. Extra yaw tuned from 20deg -> 8deg by screenshot so the head is centered and not cropped by the stage's right edge. AIM_HEIGHT raised 0.55 -> 0.62 so the aim sits nearer the shoulders/head. EVIDENCE: docs/fixes/before-pet-1280.png (fully side-on, head not visible) vs docs/fixes/after-pet-1280.png (clear front/three-quarter, head/muzzle/ears facing camera). Reduced-motion proof: docs/fixes/after-pet-reduced-1280.png.
findings.issue2a_chef: components/chef/ChefScene.tsx. MEASURED (temporary headless three+FBXLoader harness, deleted before commit): all 6 arm bones resolve on the SkeletonUtils-cloned FBX (Bip001_{R,L}_UpperArm/Forearm/Hand — all RESOLVED with non-zero rest rotations), gestureRef eases toward 1 while speaking (0.095->0.955->1.000 over ~0.5s at 60fps), the per-frame bone.rotation writes produce clearly non-zero offsets (rForearm.x offset oscillated up to ~0.53 rad ≈ 30deg), and matrixWorld updated every frame. So the bone-name/rig/write-path hypothesis is FALSE — the mechanics were sound. TRUE ROOT CAUSE: the OLD oscillation amplitudes (a few hundredths to ~0.22 rad) were too SUBTLE against the tucked rest pose to read within the fixed head-and-torso framing, so the user perceived 'no motion'. FIX: raised the arm oscillation amplitudes into a clearly visible, bounded range (upper arms ~0.18-0.30 rad, forearms up to ~0.55 rad, hands ~0.20-0.34 rad) so the chef obviously gesticulates while replying, without flailing/clipping through the body/hat. Propagation re-confirmed: ChefChatbot sets speaking via onStart/onEnd and passes `speaking={speaking}` to ChefScene. Reduced-motion gate kept EXACTLY (gTarget = reducedMotion ? 0 : speaking ? 1 : 0; arms damp to captured rest). EVIDENCE: runtime measurement above; docs/fixes/after-chef-1280.png shows the rest pose (harness still captures speaking=false), and the runtime proof documents the applied arm offsets while speaking.
findings.issue2b_coach: components/coach/CoachScene.tsx. HONEST NOTE: the coach is a STATIC UNRIGGED OBJ (public/models/characters/coach/coach.obj) with ZERO bones/skeleton — real arm/hand motion is physically IMPOSSIBLE and no rig was invented. Instead the existing whole-group talking motion was made clearly visible while speaking: bob amplitude 0.06 -> 0.11, sway 0.05 -> 0.09, yaw rotation 0.09 -> 0.16, forward lean 0.04 -> 0.08, plus a small added pitch nod (0.03 * sin(t*6.2)) blended into rotation.x so the coach reads as an emphatic, animated speaker. All still bounded to hold the fixed framing; the reduced-motion freeze and CameraRig math are intact. EVIDENCE: docs/fixes/after-coach-1280.png (rest pose in the fixed still, as speaking=false; motion manifests only while speaking).
findings.issue3_voices: lib/chef/chefVoice.ts + lib/coach/coachVoice.ts. Chef utterance params moved off the robotic extreme: pitch 0.7 -> 0.95, rate 0.9 -> 0.97 (the extreme low pitch was the primary 'robot' cause). Coach kept its natural rate 1.05 / pitch 1.0. BOTH pickVoice() implementations now prefer higher-quality voices and avoid the lowest-quality fallback: a qualityScore rewards remote voices (localService === false, +2) and names hinting enhanced/cloud/neural engines ('google','natural','enhanced','premium','neural','siri','wavenet','eloquence', +3); a `best()` helper picks the top-scoring candidate within each priority group (Italian->maleEnglish->anyEnglish for chef; brightEnglish->anyEnglish for coach), preserving priority order on ties so today's behaviour is unchanged when no quality signal exists. Speaking is NEVER gated on voice availability. All onStart/onEnd speaking-window callbacks and every anti-stuck-engine mitigation (conditional cancel, resume(), deferred 0-timeout speak, retained this.current, watchdog) are intact. Fully client-side, static-export safe. NO TTS dependency/audio asset/external service added. WEB-SPEECH LIMITATION (tradeoff, for the orchestrator to relay): a genuinely non-robotic NEURAL voice is NOT achievable within the Web Speech API + static export without adding a new TTS dependency/asset/service, which the hard constraint forbids. Within Web Speech we can only (a) tune pitch/rate away from the robotic extreme and (b) prefer the highest-quality voice the user's browser/OS already exposes (e.g. Google/cloud/neural voices when present). The remaining synthetic character on browsers that only ship low-quality local voices cannot be removed without such a dependency; we deliberately did NOT add one.
findings.issue4_wardrobe: components/WardrobeBuilder.tsx + components/wardrobe/WardrobeScene.tsx. Gave the 3D stage more room: grid template lg:grid-cols-[minmax(220px,260px)_1fr_minmax(220px,260px)] -> [minmax(180px,210px)_1fr_minmax(180px,210px)] (narrower side menus, wider center), gap lg:gap-4 -> lg:gap-3, padding sm:px-8 -> sm:px-6, stage min-height 420 -> 520 (both the <main> and inner stage div), container minHeight 760 -> 820. Also tightened WardrobeScene camera framing so the avatar fills the enlarged stage: camera position [0,1.35,2.6] -> [0,1.3,2.15], fov 40 -> 36. OrbitControls (minDistance 1.4, maxDistance 5, target, autoRotate gate) untouched so turntable/zoom still work and the reduced-motion autoRotate gate stays. VERIFIED at both widths: docs/fixes/after-wardrobe-390.json and -1280.json both report noHorizontalScroll=true; after-wardrobe-390.png shows stage-on-top with menus stacked full-width below and no covered controls; after-wardrobe-1280.png shows the avatar filling the stage prominently.
findings.ws_preservation: WS1-WS4 preserved: asset() still wraps every public URL touched (no new bare paths added); components/three/quality.ts High/Fast + the single QualityToggle untouched; ACESFilmicToneMapping unchanged on all four scenes; clicks still route through engines/state/wardrobeOptions (no parallel path added); reduced-motion gating via useReducedMotion.ts intact on every scene; canvas role='img' aria-labels intact; all scenes stay behind next/dynamic { ssr:false }.
